correctness.rationale: The claimed barrier modulus follows from a unique global maximum of g_sigma(x), where x=t/(2sqrt(mu)) and x^2=sigma^(2/3)/(1+sigma^(1/3)); evaluation gives the closed form. The state-displacement modulus is the integral of an even strictly unimodal derivative over an interval centered at zero; equality occurs at t=-h/2. The KKT perturbation norm equals the largest inequality-diagonal coefficient difference, so the triangle bound and cap at one follow. The one-constraint Q=A=1 instance gives exact sharpness with a nonsingular matrix. A frozen-solve residual is exactly (J1-J0)z, yielding the stated sufficient bound; no algorithmic convergence is asserted. The standalone script passed 10,565 seeded/deterministic checks, but finite tests are not substituted for the analytic proof.

value.rationale: Exact factorization reuse is a motivated numerical QP issue. The theorem replaces a trivial unit-coefficient bound with sharp analytic shrink- and state-dependent budgets. It exposes a non-vanishing transition-layer perturbation even at arbitrarily small barrier, which changes when one may safely rely on small matrix drift. The KKT error-to-forcing inequality yields a testable sufficient certificate when the frozen smallest singular value is estimated. The dimension-independent sharp scalar constants and their explicit attainability justify precise reuse screening, independent of any unproved global solver advantage.
